summary: Safeguarded unwind for optimizer feature-flag that caused increased tail latency and 5xxs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported a sudden increase in tail latency and intermittent 5xx responses after enabling a tenant-scoped optimizer feature-flag that changed batching and KV-prefetch behavior for quantized models. The flag was rolled out to a small percentage of traffic and then increased to 30% before the anomalies were noticed.

Impact:
- ~15% of requests from the customer's production traffic saw P95 latency jump from ~220ms to ~1.2s and P99 to ~3s.
- A subset of requests returned 502/504 when the serving process returned an internal error while loading quantized kernels.
- Customer reports increased error rate affecting business-critical inference pipelines.

Environment:
- Customer: Acme Analytics (dedicated, us-east cluster)
- Model: redwood/gpt-small-quant8 pinned at v2026-02-26
- Platform: Dedicated pool ID dp-acme-02, runtime version 3.4.1

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Tenant scoped feature-flag enablement applied at 2026-03-12T09:10:00Z to toggle "optimizer_combined_mode" on for 10% traffic.
2) Traffic increased to 30% at 2026-03-12T09:40:00Z.
3) By 09:55, SLO alerts fired for latency and error rate.
4) Attempts to increase batch_size and enable kv-prefetch for quant8 were applied via config change in console.

Observed logs / links:
- Grafana request P95 dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/reqs/acme-p95
- Error traces (sample): request-id=acme-20260312-0917-3b4e, stack shows "kernel_selection_error: unsupported kernel for quant8 path"
- SRE alert runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Latency+Incident+Runbook

Immediate customer request:
They want clear, low-risk steps to revert the optimizer flag and related config changes, including any stateful caches or long-lived worker state that must be cleaned to avoid a repeat when the flag is re-enabled later.

Desired outcome:
- Restore baseline latency and error rates for affected tenant within the SLA window.
- Provide a reproducible, documented unwind procedure the customer can run with minimal service disruption.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:05 - Support: Confirmed timing of flag rollout with customer; flag was tenant-scoped and controlled through console toggles.
2026-03-12 10:28 - SRE: Observed increased kernel selection failures in serving logs for quant8 models on nodes gpux-03 and gpux-07 in dp-acme-02.
2026-03-12 11:00 - Eng (runtime): Kernel registry returned fallback path but fallback attempted an unsupported fused-attention kernel which causes an exception under current quant path.

Hypothesis: The combination of aggressive batching + kv-prefetch for quantized execution surfaces an untested kernel selection edge-case. The feature-flag enabled a different batching heuristic that increased sequence concurrency and triggered the incompatible kernel path.
Temporary mitigation already attempted: Partial traffic rollback to 10% reduced errors but latency remained elevated; full disable not yet performed at time of report.

SRE (Miguel) 2026-03-12T10:30Z: Looking into serving logs and node-level failures; tagging gpux-03/gpux-07. Will validate which processes still have the old kernel cache loaded.

Recommending an ordered unwind: 1) disable tenant flag, 2) drain affected workers, 3) clear per-worker kernel cache (kv-store), 4) restart workers to ensure fresh kernel registry loads. resolution:
Resolution steps executed on 2026-03-12:
1) Disabled tenant-scoped feature-flag 'optimizer_combined_mode' via console (2026-03-12T12:12Z).
2) Performed rolling drain of dp-acme-02 worker set (max 2 workers at a time), cleared per-worker kernel cache (/var/lib/redwood/kernel_cache) and restarted runtime processes on each drained node.
3) Verified that kernel-selection exceptions ceased and P95/P99 returned to baseline within two rolling cycles.
4) Kept traffic at 5% for 30 minutes and then restored normal routing.

Follow-up actions and recommendations provided to customer:
- Do not re-enable combined optimizer mode until runtime patch is deployed (PR linked).
- If re-enabling is needed, do so behind a stricter canary (1% traffic), disable aggressive kv-prefetch, and monitor kernel-selection metrics closely.
- For tenant ops, include explicit worker drain + kernel cache clear in the rollback checklist to avoid stale kernel state.

- SRE to produce a short runbook snippet for dedicated pools showing how to safely clear kernel cache and drain workers - owner: Miguel Santos - ETA 2026-03-16.
